about: The terms of the ranking in place.mjs, read once at start. Another file for one run: --weights file.json; one term: --set weights.enlarge.softFrom=1.4. Every term is { value, unit, says }; only value is read. Three things rank before any cost. A candidate with a hard problem stands behind every candidate without one. One that leaves a need unmet (a text without a place, a screen's text too small to read) stands behind every one that meets them all. And where the caller names no speaker, a crop that leaves a person out of the picture stands behind every candidate that shows them all: whom to leave out is the caller's decision (--speaker), no weight makes it. Among the rest the smaller cost wins: cost = enlargement + ground + subject (a face smaller or larger than published talking heads keep theirs) + soft problems + text away + hook smaller, all in points. One point is what ten per cent of the frame as ground costs with these values. Two candidates of the same cost: the one nearer to the fit's usual hold (centred) comes first.
basis: Set by hand on 2026-11-17 from one judged case (a 1280x720 wide take into 9:16, stills looked at by people: 1.5x crisp, 1.875x mildly soft but fine, 2.67x too soft to publish, the whole picture as a strip leaves the person tiny), from stills of one upright phone take laid out by hand, and, for the size of a face, from a measurement of 240 published Shorts. The rest are guesses, each marked in its term. The measurement says what creators do, not what works.

softFrom.says: Up to here enlarging the source costs nothing and is no problem; over it the candidate carries a soft problem and the cost starts. 1.5x was judged crisp.

forbiddenFrom.says: Over this a candidate has a hard problem and ranks behind every candidate without one. 1.875x was judged fine and 2.67x too soft to publish; nothing between them was judged, 2 is a guess between them.

costAtForbidden.says: What enlargement costs at forbiddenFrom; from softFrom it rises to this in a straight line (1.875x costs 2.25 with these three values). Over about 3.3 the crisp square would pass the mildly soft 4:5 crop in the judged case: the two are a quarter of a point apart, and nobody judged which of them should lead.

from.unit: per cent of the frame's height
from.says: A face at least this tall, and at most `to`, costs nothing: it is the band published talking heads keep. Hairline to chin measured 23.2 / 26.1 / 33.6 % of the frame's height (first quartile, median, third) in 49 talking heads and 23.1 / 28.7 / 33.7 % in 60 podcast clips, of 240 published Shorts (layout study of 2026-11-17, its findings, section 5; the boxes were checked by eye). This is what is usual, not what works: nothing in that study separates the videos that did well from the others.

to.unit: per cent of the frame's height
to.says: The band's upper end: the third quartile of the same measurement (33.6 and 33.7 %). A larger face earns nothing: before the study the ranking rewarded a face up to 50 % of the frame's height, which no published video supports.

smaller.unit: points per per cent of the frame's height
smaller.says: What a face smaller than the band costs, for every per cent it falls short of `from` (the smallest face of several, its usual size when it moves). Set so that the judged order of the wide take comes out: the whole picture as a strip, the person 11 % of the frame tall, stands behind both crops.

larger.unit: points per per cent of the frame's height
larger.says: What a face larger than the band costs, for every per cent over `to`: a sixth of `smaller`. Small on purpose: a close take zoomed in a little to clear the apps' buttons must still stand before the same take made smaller over a ground, as the layout made by hand has it (at 0.1 the smaller picture with slivers of ground led by a hair). A guess: no case decides it.

regionEnough.unit: per cent of the frame's width or height
regionEnough.says: A screen's region has no measured band. It is the better the more of the frame's width or height it spans (whichever is more), up to this share; every per cent short of it costs `smaller`. A guess: no case decides it.

cost.unit: points per per cent of the frame
cost.says: What visible ground costs: for every per cent of the frame that the sharp picture does not fill (the blurred copy behind a smaller picture, a band above and below a crop, the side of a panel).
What a soft problem other than enlargement costs: a face or text in the safe box's margin, cut by a feed's crop, another person's face cut by a crop's edge.

away.says: What it costs to set a text away from its usual place (captions: at the safe box's bottom, then in the picture's bottom, beside the face, above the head, on the ground above; hook: at the top). Small on purpose: it only orders holds of the same picture.

hookSmaller.says: What a hook set smaller than its size costs. Small on purpose: the larger picture with a smaller hook comes before the smaller picture with the full one; both are listed.
